sections.h2: Who mails the Colquitt County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner in Moultrie mails and collects the bill. Value belongs to the Tax Assessor's Office, and the commissioner's own site says that office sets neither the value nor the millage rate.

The counter sits at 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie, GA 31768. The postal box is number 99. Staff work weekdays from 8:00am until 4:30pm, and the property tax line is (229) 616-7410. The same office runs motor vehicle registration, and a separate solid waste desk at 101 East Central Avenue, Office 168, is reached at (229) 616-7405. The landfill opens Saturday mornings from 8:00am to noon, which matters if you are clearing a house before listing it.

  • Tax Assessor's Office: appraisal, assessment notices and exemption approvals.
  • Board of Equalization: administrative appeals, with members named by the grand jury.
  • County commission and school board: each levies its own mill rate.
  • Tax Commissioner: bills, payments, liens and levies.

sections.h2: What does Colquitt County look like around Moultrie?
sections.html:
Colquitt County is a Southwest Georgia farming county of about 557 square miles, created on February 25, 1856. Moultrie holds the courthouse and is the biggest city, and the county's western side drains toward the Ochlockonee River while the central and eastern parts drain toward the Withlacoochee and Little River basins.

The county touches Tift, Cook, Brooks, Thomas, Mitchell and Worth counties. Gray Lake and Lake Murphy are its named lakes, and Autreyville, Barbers, Hartsfield, Murphy and Riverside are listed as unincorporated communities. In Moultrie, US 319 runs to Interstate 75 about 24 miles east, and Reed Bingham State Park and the Tom White Linear Park trail are local landmarks. The Colquitt County School District operates elementary schools named for Doerun, Funston and Norman Park.

QuickFacts reports 47,438 people in its 2025 estimate and 19,775 housing units. Owners occupy 63.7% of homes. The Census five-year estimate puts a typical owned home at $121,400, gross rent at $818 and household income at $49,341.

sections.h2: When do Colquitt County bills fall due?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property are normally due December 10, and the commissioner's site says bills are mailed at least 60 days before that. Follow whatever date your own bill prints, since the page warns it may change.

Tax bills are addressed to the owner, not the lender. A homeowner whose mortgage does not escrow must pass the bill along. The office also cannot promise a bill reaches you, and it says interest, penalty and costs apply regardless.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow their own deadline, and the county's two pages give different dates for it. Call the tax commissioner and ask which applies to your unit. A mobile home moving into or out of the county needs a relocation permit first, from the Compliance office in the Courthouse Annex, reached at 229-616-7417.

sections.h2: How are late bills handled in Colquitt County?
sections.html:
A bill left past the due date draws interest each month, and later a penalty. The county's pages describe the exact rates differently, so ask for a written payoff instead of working it out yourself. The site does say the penalty skips homesteaded property whose bill is under $500.

If the tax stays unpaid, a tax lien called a FiFa goes on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court. The site says it stays on a credit record for at least seven years, and that the commissioner may levy and eventually sell the property. It describes levy as a last resort.

The office mails delinquent notices only at certain intervals. That means the amount on the last notice you saw may be out of date by the time you pay or close.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax if the house sells in Colquitt County?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner stays on the bill and on any lien, even if the deed changes hands in June. A seller can move that to the buyer by putting the closing statement in the commissioner's hands by day 90 after the due date.

The office spells out the mechanics. If your closing prorated the tax, bring the settlement statement to the office on East Central Avenue. With that in hand it can record a lien against the new owner if the bill remains unpaid. A bill that arrives for a house you already sold should be forwarded to the buyer.

Find out from the title company how the county gets paid, then ask the commissioner for a payoff dated near the closing. Selling with a recorded lien is workable, because the payoff is settled at the closing table and comes out of the sale funds.

sections.h2: What exemptions and programs does Colquitt County list?
sections.html:
The commissioner's site lists a standard exemption and several age, veteran and income-based ones, all subtracted from the assessed value, which Georgia fixes at 40% of fair market value. The first application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, and first-time owners are told to bring a copy of the warranty deed. Georgia requires it to be received by April 1.

  • Standard homestead: printed as $2,000 off assessed value, for county, school system and state levies.
  • Elderly school tax, age 62 or older: up to $10,000 off, with net income of $10,000 or less.
  • Elderly general, age 65 or older: up to $4,000 off, with a $10,000 income test that excludes Social Security and some retirement income.
  • Disabled veteran and qualifying surviving spouse: up to $63,780 off.
  • Floating exemption: age 62 or older with gross household income of $30,000 or less, covering state and county tax but not school tax.

Colquitt County also has local exemptions that override the state amounts when larger, so the assessors can tell you what applies today. Farmland has its own paths: assessment at 30% for bona fide agricultural use, and conservation use or timber programs that require a covenant of at least 10 years. Historic property and certain hazardous-site redevelopment parcels may also qualify. Owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less can defer tax until a sale or until the deferral and interest reach 85% of fair market value.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Colquitt County value?
sections.html:
Put the appeal in writing, and do it inside 45 days counted from the date on the assessment notice. The county FAQ names two routes, equalization board or arbitrator, and says either result can be carried on to Superior Court.

Each spring, up to April 1, you may also file a return stating your own opinion of the property's January 1 value. An owner who stays silent is treated as returning the same value and exemptions as the year before. For a mobile home the county page allows 45 days to appeal to the assessors, then 21 days from their notice to reach the equalization board.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Colquitt County property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's office, 101 East Central Ave., Moultrie. Staff work weekdays from 8:00am to 4:30pm, and the card payments carry a convenience fee from the card company.

faqs.q: What date is Colquitt County property tax normally due?
faqs.a: December 10 for real estate and business personal property. Your bill's printed date is the one to trust, because the commissioner says it may change.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Colquitt County house with a recorded tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff is settled from the sale funds at closing, so request a current figure from the commissioner and hand it to the title company.

faqs.q: Which Colquitt County office takes homestead applications?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's Office. Georgia requires the application to be received by April 1, and a later filing counts toward the next tax year.

faqs.q: What is the appeal window for a Colquitt County assessment?
faqs.a: 45 days counted from the date on the notice. You can ask for the equalization board or an arbitrator, and Superior Court is open afterward.
